cycles.name: Foundation Forge
cycles.tagline: Earn the right to be fast.
focuses: Rebuild the lifting base from zero and find your real numbers on the squat and trap bar — top sets filmed in weeks 1 and 2 before any weight moves.
Start the ankle, groin and shoulder work that keeps you on court, and report a sleep number every week — that's the biggest lever you have right now.

paragraphs: You told me two things that matter. You don't get tired in padel, but your errors go up as the match goes on. And you feel strong but slow. Those are the same problem. Your body knows how to make force. It doesn't know how to make it fast yet, and it stops making it cleanly once you've been on court an hour.

We don't fix that by throwing speed drills at a body that hasn't lifted in a while. These five weeks rebuild the base and find your real numbers. Nothing heavy, nothing you have to grind through. Week 1 you'll feel underworked. That's on purpose.
By the end of this you'll have a base we can make fast.
outcomes: Real working numbers on the squat and trap bar
Top sets filmed in weeks 1 and 2 and cleared before the weight moves
A sleep number reported to me every week
Three gym sessions a week without wrecking your padel
Five weeks of ankle and Achilles springiness banked
Groin work in the bank before the season loads up

cycles.name: Strength Reclaim
focuses: Re-express heavy strength with speed intent — every working rep accelerated, bar speed is the target, never the grind.
Build the eccentric and deceleration capacity that gets you to the ball balanced instead of braking late.
cycles.teaser:
Cycle 2 is where you take the strength back. Same body, heavier bar, one rule that changes everything: every rep moves fast or it doesn't count.

You earn it here first. Five clean weeks and the brakes come off.

The powerlifter is still in there. We're going to teach him to move.

cycles.name: Power Transfer
focuses: Turn that strength into rate of force development — heavy work contrasted with jumps and throws.
Rotational power and hip-shoulder separation for the shot.

cycles.name: Spring Steel
focuses: Reactive strength and change-of-direction speed — the quality you mean when you say you feel slow.
Hold your strength at a minimum effective dose so nothing built earlier leaks away.

cycles.name: Closing Speed
cycles.tagline: As fast in the third set.
focuses: Repeat-effort power — hold your movement speed and shot quality deep into a match, where your errors live.
Consolidate: strength and reactivity maintained, everything pointed at on-court transfer.

cards.title: Why You Feel Slow
cards.body:
You said your body feels slow, and that it started after you lost the weight. Let me be straight with you about that. Losing that weight was real work and it was the right call for padel. What you're feeling now isn't the weight coming back to bite you.

Here's what I think is going on. Years of powerlifting taught your body to make a lot of force slowly. Padel needs force in a quarter of a second, again and again. You have the engine, you've just never trained the part that makes it fast.

The other half is that you haven't lifted in a while and you're sleeping five hours. Heavy and slow all day is exactly what that feels like. We fix the training here and we work on the sleep at the same time.

cards.title: How To Pick Your Weight
cards.body:
I don't give you a weight to lift, you find it. Every exercise tells you the reps and an RPE number, and RPE just means how hard the set should feel. RPE 7 means you finish the set knowing you had about three more reps in you.

For a movement you haven't done before, start too light on purpose. Do the first set, see how it felt, then go up. Better to waste one set than to pick wrong and grind.

Week to week it's simple:

  • Hit all your reps and it felt at or under the target RPE, add a small jump next week.
  • RPE was at the ceiling or you missed reps, keep the same weight and do it again.
  • Bad sleep, hard match yesterday, feeling flat, drop the weight. That isn't failure, that's the system working.

Week 1 you go light everywhere. You should walk out of the gym thinking you could have done more. You've got three padel days to protect.

cards.title: Film Your Top Sets
cards.body:
I've never seen you lift. You told me you did powerlifting for years and I believe you, but I'm not standing next to you and your body has had a break from the gym.

Film your heaviest set of the Back Squat and the Trap Bar Deadlift in week 1 and week 2 and send them to me on WhatsApp. Film from the side, whole body in the frame.

The weight goes up on those two once I've seen the film and cleared it. If the videos stop coming, the weight stops moving. That's the deal.

cards.title: Sleep Is Your First Lift
cards.body:
You're on five to six hours and you rated the quality five out of ten. I'll be honest with you. That's the single biggest thing holding you back right now, bigger than any exercise in this program.

That heavy feeling in the day, and the errors piling up late in a match, both live there. Your body repairs and your brain sharpens on sleep. Six hours doesn't cover a man lifting three times a week and playing padel four.

I'm not asking for eight tomorrow. Add thirty minutes. Same bedtime every night for these five weeks, phone out of the room. Tell me the number every week, not how it felt.

cards.title: Gym Days That Are Padel Days
cards.body:
Most weeks the gym and the court land on the same day. Here's the rule.

  • Lift after padel, not before. Never walk onto court with heavy legs.
  • If you can split them, leave four to six hours between.
  • If neither works and you're squeezed, do the first two exercises of that day only and keep the main lift easier. That still counts as a session.

The order of days is a suggestion, move them around your court time. Just try not to put Day 1 and Day 3 back to back, they're the two heavy ones.

cards.title: You're Training Now, Eat Like It
cards.body:
You said your eating is average and not consistent. You've finished losing weight, so from here the job is different. You're not cutting any more, you're feeding training.

Two things only for these five weeks. Protein at every meal, a palm-sized portion or more, three or four times a day. And don't lift or play on an empty stomach, something small an hour before is enough.

I'm not giving you numbers yet. Get those two steady, tell me how it went at the check-in, and then we get specific.

cards.title: Week 5 Eases Off
cards.body:
Weeks 1 to 4 are the work. Week 5 is a back-off week and it's part of the plan, not a break you earned or lost.

In week 5 keep the same exercises and the same weights, but take one set off each of your main lifts and stop every set earlier than usual. Leave four or five reps in the tank instead of three. Easy on purpose.

The cards don't change. They show your normal target for the whole cycle. Week 5 is the one week you ignore the number and go light.
